# Formal divisor class groups of oriented symmetric products of projective space

## Finding
For integers \(n\geq 2\), \(d\geq5\), let \(A_d\) act on \(T=(\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C})^d\) by even permutations of the factors, and put \(Y=T/A_d\). Every closed point \(y\in Y\) is represented by a tuple whose equal-value blocks have sizes \(\lambda=(m_1,\ldots,m_s)\), with \(\sum m_i=d\). Let \(r=\#\{i:m_i\geq2\}\).

**Theorem.** The normal projective variety \(Y\) is locally factorial, Gorenstein, terminal and Fano, with \(\operatorname{Cl}(Y)=\operatorname{Pic}(Y)\cong\mathbb Z\), generated by the descent \(H\) of \(\boxtimes_{j=1}^d\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n}(1)\), and \(-K_Y=(n+1)H\). Nevertheless its completed local divisor class groups have the exact partition-stratified form
\[
\operatorname{Cl}(\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y,y})\cong
\begin{cases}
0,&r=0,\\
\mathbb Z/3,&r=1\text{ and the unique }m_i\geq2\text{ equals }3\text{ or }4,\\
0,&r=1\text{ and that }m_i=2\text{ or }m_i\geq5,\\
(\mathbb Z/2)^{r-1},&r\geq2.
\end{cases}
\]
In particular a single triple collision has nontrivial formal \(3\)-torsion, and two disjoint double collisions have formal \(2\)-torsion, although **every algebraic local ring of \(Y\) is a UFD**. The formula completely determines the formal factorial locus on every collision stratum.

## Assumptions and scope
The ground field is \(\mathbb C\); all groups and Chow/divisor classes are ordinary (not stacky) unless explicitly specified. The quotient \(Y\) is the coarse geometric quotient by the alternating group on factor labels. Collision blocks consist of equal points of \(\mathbb P^n\); distinct blocks have distinct points. The completion is at a **closed complex point**. Factorial means algebraically locally factorial; formally factorial means the completed local ring is a UFD. The source motivating the symmetric-power family is Chen–Hu, arXiv:2610.20239v1 (2026-10-14; primary MSC 14C25), which considers \(T/S_d\), not the divisor-theoretic invariants of \(T/A_d\).

## Proof
**1. Divisor class group and Cartier descent.** The union \(Z\) of pairwise diagonals in \(T\) has codimension \(n\geq2\). Let \(U=T\setminus Z\), on which \(A_d\) acts freely, and let \(V=U/A_d\). Since both removed complements have codimension at least two and \(T\) is smooth,
\[
\operatorname{Cl}(Y)=\operatorname{Cl}(V)=\operatorname{Pic}(V)=\operatorname{Pic}^{A_d}(U).
\]
Here \(\operatorname{Pic}(U)=\operatorname{Pic}(T)=\mathbb Z^d\) and \(\mathcal O_U^*(U)=\mathbb C^*\) by extension across codimension two. The forgetful map from linearized bundles to invariant classes has kernel \(\operatorname{Hom}(A_d,\mathbb C^*)=0\) because \(A_d\) is perfect for \(d\geq5\); its target is \((\mathbb Z^d)^{A_d}=\mathbb Z(1,\ldots,1)\). This generator has an actual linearization: permute tensor factors of \(L=\boxtimes_j\mathcal O(1)\). At any point with nontrivial stabilizer, that permutation acts trivially on the one-dimensional tensor-product fiber because the permuted factors over each equal-point block are the *same* line. Hence the linearized \(L\) descends to an invertible sheaf \(H\) on the whole coarse quotient. Thus \(\operatorname{Cl}(Y)=\operatorname{Pic}(Y)=\mathbb Z[H]\): every Weil divisor is Cartier. Since \(L\) is ample and finite pullback reflects ampleness, \(H\) is ample. Under even permutations the natural linearization on the canonical bundle \(\omega_T=L^{-(n+1)}\) agrees with the corresponding tensor permutation: the permutation's top-wedge sign is \((\operatorname{sgn}\sigma)^n=1\). There is no divisorial ramification, so \(K_Y=-(n+1)H\).

**2. Formal quotient and its class group.** Fix an equal-point partition \(\lambda\). The stabilizer of a chosen tuple is
\[
G_\lambda=\left(\prod_{i=1}^sS_{m_i}\right)\cap A_d
=\ker\left(\prod_i S_{m_i}\xrightarrow{\prod\operatorname{sgn}}\{\pm1\}\right).
\]
Since the action is tame and \(T\) is smooth, formal linearization and the finite quotient identify \(\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y,y}\) with the invariant formal power-series algebra of the tangent representation \(\bigoplus_{j=1}^dT_{t_j}\mathbb P^n\) under \(G_\lambda\). A nonidentity element moves at least three factor labels, so its fixed tangent-space codimension is at least \(2n\geq4\); the representation contains no pseudoreflections. For a complex finite group acting linearly without pseudoreflections, the standard invariant-ring divisor-class theorem gives
\[
\operatorname{Cl}(\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y,y})\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G_\lambda,\mathbb C^*).
\]
This is the class group of the **completion**, not the local algebraic class group.

**3. Abelianization of parity kernels.** If \(r=0\), \(G_\lambda=1\). If \(r=1\), \(G_\lambda=A_m\), where \(m\) is the only block size at least two. The abelianizations of \(A_2,A_3,A_4,A_m\ (m\geq5)\) are respectively \(0,\mathbb Z/3,\mathbb Z/3,0\).

If \(r\geq2\), the product of sign maps induces
\[
1\longrightarrow\prod_{m_i\geq2}A_{m_i}\longrightarrow G_\lambda
\longrightarrow(\mathbb Z/2)^{r-1}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Every \(A_m\) for \(m\geq5\) is perfect. The only possible nontrivial abelianizations of the kernel factors are the \(3\)-groups from \(A_3\) and \(A_4\). For such a factor choose an odd permutation in that block together with an odd permutation in *another* nontrivial block. This yields an element of \(G_\lambda\) conjugating the \(3\)-torsion class to its inverse. In the abelianization, that class therefore equals its inverse, and because it has order three it vanishes. Hence the entire kernel lies in \([G_\lambda,G_\lambda]\), and the quotient \((\mathbb Z/2)^{r-1}\) is exactly the abelianization. Taking characters proves the displayed formula.

**4. Terminal and Gorenstein properties.** At any fixed point, the tangent action of \(\sigma\in A_d\) permutes \(d\) blocks of dimension \(n\). If \(c(\sigma)\) is the number of permutation cycles, its Reid–Tai age is
\[
\operatorname{age}(\sigma)=\frac n2\bigl(d-c(\sigma)\bigr).
\]
For nonidentity even permutations, \(d-c(\sigma)\geq2\) and is even. Thus every age is at least \(n\geq2>1\). Since no pseudoreflections occur, the Reid–Tai criterion yields terminal singularities. Also \(\det(\sigma\mid T_tT)=(\operatorname{sgn}\sigma)^n=1\), yielding the Gorenstein property, already reflected by the Cartier canonical class in Step 1. With \(-K_Y\) ample, \(Y\) is Fano.

## Verification
An independently executable standard-library Python script `CHECK.py` enumerates the parity kernels for representative small block profiles, forms every commutator, computes the subgroup they generate, and compares its index with the predicted abelianization cardinality. Profiles checked: \((3),(4),(5),(2,2),(2,2,2),(3,2),(4,2),(3,3),(3,4),(2,2,3)\). The calculation checks small examples only; the universal theorem is proved in Steps 1–4. Reproduce by running `python CHECK.py` from the extracted package directory.

## Relationship to prior work
Chen and Hu, *Chow groups of symmetric products of projective space* (arXiv:2610.20239v1, sections 1–4 and Appendix A), study integral cycle classes of the unordered quotient \(T/S_d\), including torsion phenomena and finite quotient transfers. They do not state the formal class-group stratification for the alternating quotient \(T/A_d\). The sign cover here is not a new construction: it is the evident intermediate quotient. Geraschenko and Satriano, *Torus quotients as global quotients by finite groups* (2015, section 5.1), already use quotients by perfect groups to obtain factorial quotient singularities, notably \(\mathbb P(V)/A_5\); the general methods of quotient-stack Picard groups and local formal stabilizer groups are established. Maithani, *Homological properties of invariant rings of permutation groups* (arXiv:2511.07718v2, sections 5 and 6), analyzes Gorenstein and permutation invariant-ring properties, not this geometric partition classification. What is asserted here, subject to the priority caveat below, is the **complete explicit three-way formal divisor-class stratification and the simultaneous algebraic-versus-formal comparison** for the oriented symmetric powers of \(\mathbb P^n\).

## Limitations
This is a class-group statement over \(\mathbb C\) for closed points and \(n\geq2,d\geq5\); it does not classify completions up to ring isomorphism, higher Chow groups, cohomology, crepant resolutions or deformations. The formal divisor classes need not be algebraizations of divisors in a local Zariski neighborhood. The group-theoretic and invariant-ring lemmas are classical: an undiscovered earlier explicit formulation could establish the same classification. The result makes no independent-priority certification claim.
